title: Fixed Windows Meeting an Average Bar
statement:
You get an array arr of positive integers, a window size k and a number threshold. Look at every block of exactly k consecutive elements.

Return how many of those blocks have an average of at least threshold. The average is the exact value, not rounded.

examples.why: The block sums are 9, 12, 8 and 11. Only 12 / 3 = 4 reaches the bar; 11 / 3 ≈ 3.67 does not.
The one block averages exactly 2, and reaching the bar counts.
[5, 6] averages 5.5, which rounds to 6 but is below it. Only [6, 7] counts.

hints: Summing each block from scratch is O(n · k). Neighboring blocks share k − 1 elements.
Slide the window: add the element that enters and subtract the one that leaves.
Compare sum ≥ k · threshold instead of dividing. It is exact and avoids floating-point worries.

explain.intuition:
A block of size k and the block one step to the right share k − 1 elements. So keep a running sum: add the element entering on the right, subtract the one leaving on the left. Each block's sum then costs O(1) instead of O(k).

The average test sum / k ≥ threshold is the same as sum ≥ k · threshold, because k is positive. Multiplying keeps everything in integers, so there is no rounding to get wrong.
steps: If i ≥ k, subtract arr[i − k], the element that just left.
pitfalls: Rounding the average. In [5, 6] the average 5.5 rounds to 6 but is below a bar of 6.
Counting a window before it has k elements.
Using > instead of ≥: an average exactly at the bar counts.

solutions.title: Sum every block
solutions.idea: For each start, add up the next k elements and test the sum.

solutions.title: Sliding window sum
solutions.idea: Keep the sum of the last k elements: add the newcomer, drop the element k steps back.

followups: Answer the same question for many different thresholds at once. What do you sort?
Count windows of any length at least k whose average reaches the bar. (Hint: subtract threshold from every element.)
lcTitle: Number of Sub-arrays of Size K and Average Greater than or Equal to Threshold
